Allergies:
No Known Allergies / Adverse Drug Reactions

Chief Complaint:
Shortness of breath

History of Present Illness:
___ with PMHx CAD (last LHC ___ with mid-RCA 60% stenosis 
medically managed), HFpEF, AF (not on AC due to hx of GIB), and 
COPD who presents from ___ where she presented with 
increased dyspnea.

Per patient, Ms. ___ has had chronic dyspnea which worsened 
progressively over the last 3 weeks. She is usually able to walk 
"about 10 feet" but was only able to walk a few steps before 
having to catch her breath for some time. She sleeps with 6 
pillows at baseline due to GERD, however notes orthopnea and 
episodes of PND over the past week. She denies any chest pain 
both at home and at ___ but does endorse some burning 
epigastric pain "that feels like heartburn." No associated 
diaphorises, nausea or vomiting. 

At ___ she was found to be hypoxic with CXR showing 
pulmonary edema and was diuresed with 40 mg IV Lasix, given 
steroids for possible COPD exacerbation, and transfused 1U pRBC 
for anemia. She developed AF with RVR with associated STD in 
anterolateral leads with TropI 18.1 and CKMB 81.3. She was 
transferred to their ICU where she continued to be diuresed and 
RHC performed with CVP 24, PAP 74/28, PCWP 36, CO/CI 4.3/2.1. PA 
catheter was left in place. Given concern for ongoing ischemia 
and decompensated CHF, she was transferred to ___ for further 
management.

On arrival to the CCU, she continues to endorse SOB. Denies any 
CP, LH, nausea, abdominal pain, or bloody stools. She states 
that her legs are more edematous and that her weight has 
increased. Otherwise, no complaints. 

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
Positive per HPI, otherwise negative.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: ___ with PMHx CAD, HFpEF, AF and COPD who 
presents from ___ with increased dyspnea c/w decompensated 
CHF in setting of NSTEMI.

#NSTEMI: She was given Aspirin 81mg, Metoprolol tartrate 25mg 
q6h (fractionated from her home dose of 100mg daily), and 
Atorvastatin 80mg daily, and maintained on a Heparin drip 
(titrated to a goal PTT of 50-80) until 48 hours after her 
NSTEMI. Her cardiac biomarkers were trended until peak. 

#Acute decompensated heart failure: The etiology of her heart 
failure was felt to be in the setting of ischemia due to 
patients known CAD and recent NSTEMI. For preload reduction, she 
was diuresed with Lasix until euvolemic. She had previously 
taken Lisinopril at home, but this was held during admission due 
to concern for acute kidney injury. For contractility, she was 
given Metoprolol as above.

#acute hypoxemic respiratory failure: Likely multifactorial, due 
to decompensated heart failure as above as well as patient's 
known COPD. She initially treated for COPD exacerbation at OSH 
but was found to be remarkably fluid overloaded. Due a concern 
for HCAP, she was treated with broad spectrum coverage 
(Vancomycin and Cefepime, ___ and Flagyll, 
___. On presentation to the CCU, she 
required 8L NC, and occasionally a non-rebreather. However, this 
improved with diuresis and she was able to wean back to 2L NC. 
She was continued on her home inhalers/nebulizers (Duonebs, 
Albuterol, Spiriva). On the morning of ___, she was noted to 
have acute chest pressure and dyspnea. She was hypotensive to 
SBPs ___. EKG showed ischemic changes in AVR, II, III. It was 
noted that she has had similar ischemic changes when 
tachycardic/hypotensive. She was diuresed due to concern for 
continued pulmonary edema, but otherwise no intervention was 
made.

#Afib: She has a history of A-fib, and tried a cardioversion in 
___. She has declined anticoagulation in past secondary to 
epistaxis and GI bleed. She was rate controlled with Metoprolol 
as above; and was not found to be in RVR during admission. She 
was not anticoagulated other than with Heparin for her NSTEMI.

#Anemia: Hemoglobin 8.3 on admission after transfusion with 1 
uPRBcs at the outside hospital for a hemoglobin of 7.3. Fecal 
occult blood testing was performed and was negative. Iron 
studies were performed (see results above), and she was started 
on IV Iron for a 7 day course, for a presumed iron deficiency 
anemia. A hemolytic work-up including Haptoglobin and fibrinogen 
was initiated but was unremarkable.

#Flank pain. She was intermittently complaining of flank pain 
early in her admission. A renal ultrasound was obtained which 
revealed a non-obstructing stone. However, this was not on the 
same side as her symptoms. Urology was consulted, they felt that 
the stone did not need to be intervened on. 

#Diabetes mellitus type II: She was continued on her home 
novalog 70:30 and Insulin sliding scale.

#CKD: Her baseline creatinine appeared to be 1.5-2. During 
admission, her Cr peaked to as high as 2.3, presumed to be due 
to cardiorenal acute kidney injury. Her creatinine improved with 
diuresis. 

#UTI: Patient with positive UA on admission in ___. Given 2 
days of ceftriaxone. Currently asymptomatic. She completed a 3 
course of ceftriaxone 1 g Q24, last dose ___. 

===============
After stabilization in the CCU, she was transferred to the heart 
failure service on ___ with the following course: 

# Acute decompensated heart failure, HFpEF (EF 60%): Diuresed 
with Lasix IV boluses until dry and then switched to torsemide 
with goal of net even I/O. She became hypotensive with low UOP 
and tors was held and IVF were given. Restarted on torsemide 
40mg daily, metoprolol XL 25mg and lisinopril 5mg daily at 
discharge. 

#acute hypoxemic respiratory failure: resolved at discharge. Pt 
completed antibiotic coverage for HCAP (see ICU course above). 
She experienced fluctuating dyspnea with increased sputum 
production later in hospital course c/f PNA vs COPD 
exacerbation. Afebrile with no leukocytosis and no PNA on CXR. 
Fungal workup was negative. COPD exacerbation was most likely. 
She was treated with nebs and weaned off O2 by discharge.  B/l 
pleural effusions (R>L) improved greatly. 

#CAD - Left heart cath ___ with BMS in RCA and residual 60% 
stenosis at ostium LAD.  No intervention was performed on LAD 
due to location and patient tolerability during cath. Concern  
for residual disease in LAD following first LHC and PCI prompted 
a p-MIBI on ___ which showed no ischemic changes or perfusion 
defects.  Pt remained CP free following first PCI.  She will 
follow up with cardiology as outpatient. 

#UTI -On admission, she had a grossly positive UA and a CTU scan 
showing moderate hydroureteronephrosis secondary to a 9 mm 
calculus noted in the left distal ureter. Urology did not feel 
that a perc neph tube was needed and recommended ___ 
Urology f/u. She was started on Flomax. She had a positive urine 
Cx on ___ growing 100K CFU of e. coli with more incontinence. In 
the setting of a stone, she was treated with 7 days of 
Cefpodoxime. 

# Gout: patient with left knee pain, warmth and erythema and 
history of gout. Declined arthrocentesis. Started on colchicine 
___ and uptitrated to 0.6 mg BID. Recommended to have Uric acid 
drawn about 2 weeks after complete resolution.  

#Anemia: Hemoglobin 8.3 on admission after transfusion with 1 
unit PRBcs. Patient was 7.3 on presentation to OSH. Transfused 
with total of 5 units pRBCs during admission. Initially, 
etiology of her iron deficiency anemia thought to be due to 
multiple episodes of epistaxis as well as frequent blood draws 
and hemolysis labs unremarkable. However patient required 
multiple transfusions of pRBCs after leaving the CCU. She 
developed melena prompting an EGD on ___ revealing a Dieulafoy 
lesion in duodenal bulb. This was cauterized successfully 
without residual bleeding and her H&H stabilized. 

# NSTEMI: see CAD above. Pt s/p BMS in RCA and 60% LAD stenosis 
with no evidence of anginal sx, ST changes, or perfusion defects 
on f/u p-MIBI. She was discharged on ___, metoprolol XL, 
and atorvastatin. 

# Acute on CKD: Baseline Cr per report 1.5-2. Peaked to 1.8 at 
___. Responded well to euvolemia returning to 1.5 at 
discharge. 
 
# Afib: Patient with history of atrial fib s/p cardioversion in 
___ but currently rate controlled. Although she has a CHADS 
VASC of at least 3, she has declined anticoagulation in the past 
___ epistaxis and GIB. She stopped warfarin in ___. AC not 
advisable currently given GIB on this admission. She remained 
rate controlled with metoprolol 25mg XL daily. 

CHRONIC/RESOLVED ISSUES:
# DM II: Home novalog 70:30 and Insulin sliding scale. A1c 6.0 
on ___. Decreased eve dose to 40 on ___ due to symptomatic 
hypoglycemia. 

Transitional Issues
Started on ___ a 7 day Cefpodoxime course for complicated UTI. 
Discharged on Toresemide 40 mg daily. 
Dry Weight: 96.4 kg. 
Discharge Cr: 1.5
Should be on a PPI BID for ___ weeks and transition to daily.

with more incontinence. In the setting of a stone we elected to

-She developed knee pain that was consistent with gout. Consider 
checking uric acid level within 2 weeks of discharge and 
starting Allopurinol. 
-Please evaluate for home 02. 
-She is being discharged with ___ and home ___ 
-Should have Chem 10 and CBC checked at follow up
